name: fire
title: How Did Cavemen Make Fire? (400,000-Year-Old Sparks!)

lines: The oldest proof of people making fire was found in England.
And it's about four hundred thousand years old.
So how did cavemen make fire?
Meet Moss. He's rubbing sticks. Nothing.
Surprise one: using fire is even older.
In Wonderwerk Cave, South Africa, there's ash and burnt bone from about a million years ago.
But using fire isn't making it.
Maybe they grabbed flames from wildfires.
Surprise two: at Barnham, people lit fires in one spot, again and again.
It got hotter than seven hundred degrees.
Surprise three: two little pieces of a rock called pyrite.
Strike it with flint, and you get sparks.
Pyrite isn't found naturally there.
So someone probably brought it, to start fires.
Who? Experts think early Neanderthals.
Surprise four: Neanderthals in France left clues too.
Scratches on their hand axes suggest striking pyrite for sparks.
Rubbing sticks? Maybe. But wood rots, so there's no proof that old.
Moss tried pyrite. A spark! Right onto his hair.
